\chapter{What the evidence changes about the proposed service}
\label{rewrite:evidence-consequences}

The four journeys distinguish a wrong target, insufficient treatment support,
causal ambiguity and uncertain measurement. Those failures demand different
responses. A common service should make the distinctions visible while
reusing the appropriate statistical procedures. Its initial scope follows
from the evidence below; it does not require every possible capability to
be implemented at once.

\section{A result should change a design choice}
The existing 3,000-replication generated offer study is evidence about target
alignment. Under one specified design, the residual projection averages
26.447 when the equal-population benefit is 50. Its interval covers its own
target in 97.2\% of repetitions and the population target in none. At the
stipulated cost of 40, interpreting it as the population effect rejects the
beneficial offer in all 500 repetitions of that scenario. The design
consequence is to put the population weights and target in the result,
and to compare implementations only after aligning those quantities. A
more precise projection is not a repair for this interpretation error.

The separate 6,000-replication sparse-support study addresses inference
after the target is aligned. Pooling yields 94.7\% conditional coverage
under equal normal variances but 52.2\% under the tested unequal-variance
case. Cellwise Student intervals joined by a union bound preserve the
conditional coverage guarantee in the normal model at the cost of very
wide intervals. Thus the initial implementation should show cell support
and retain an unsupported or inconclusive result. If useful precision
requires unjustified pooling, the next expenditure should improve assignment
support or the information collected. These are existing generated
experiments, not evidence of superiority by a named external package.

contact records, later-archive prediction has AUC 0.630 using the candidate
pre-call feature set and 0.793 when duration is added. The latter feature
is unavailable before the call, so its predictive gain cannot justify
pre-call targeting. Differences between early and late archive outcomes
also matter for evaluation. The correct service response is to preserve
availability dates and the evaluation period. Neither score estimates
the effect of making a call. Chapter~\ref{scisyn:evidence} gives the
executed design, comparators, results and qualifications.

instrument, design and observation restrictions remain attached to their

covariance in a public application does not validate a bank's common-calendar

expert composition and a minimal shared integration. The cases should
include correct assignment, heterogeneous effects, unequal treatment
support, unavailable predictors, misrecorded receipt and a dependent
sampling request outside the accepted route. The generated law supplies
truth where that is possible; a public case supplies realistic data handling

a completed scientific answer when the information is insufficient.

\chapter{Which tasks merit language assistance?}
\label{rewrite:assistance-tasks}

Assistance should be selected by the task it improves. A system that answers
questions about a supplied causal mechanism has not thereby shown that
it can discover a defensible mechanism for a new bank. The evidence
synthesis in Chapter~\ref{scisyn:assistance} and the detailed studies
support a restricted comparison, with a questionnaire and ordinary search
as serious alternatives. They do not establish a measured saving for this
proposed product.

\section{Formulation and variable construction}
For formulation, the useful output is a precise intervention, alternative,
population, outcome, horizon and information date, together with unresolved
choices. The retained Kıcıman and causal-learn+ discussions motivate
question clarification and graph critique. Their descriptions support
a prototype candidate, not the truth of bank-specific assumptions.
\citep{v12_la_2305_00050,v12_la_2606_23608}
The strongest elementary comparator is a structured questionnaire completed
by an economist. Measure material omissions found and the time required
to correct the final question. The deposit distinction among assignment,
receipt, acceptance and price is an explicit test case. An eloquent
answer that silently chooses one is a failure.

Variable construction requires a separate assessment. A model can suggest
a record field or an extraction rule, but measurement validity depends
on the relation between that field and the scientific variable. The
retained text-and-causal-inference review discusses text used for adjustment;
it does not prove that a modern embedding removes confounding.
\citep{exec13_census_text_review_arxiv}
Compare any proposed extraction with a documented coding rule and
independently labelled examples, preserving missing and ambiguous cases.
The observation journey shows why high predictive accuracy or apparent
completeness is insufficient. Begin with auditable field definitions and
retrieval assistance; an autonomous scientific measurement claim remains
unsupported without independent validation.

\section{Diagrams and numerical discovery}
For diagram work, require evidence and timing for each proposed relationship
and retain competing explanations. LACR's reported retrieval effects vary
across its examples. The retained inspection records both improvement and
deterioration, including the ASIA skeleton comparison and the SACHS
comparison when PC output is added. This is evidence for evaluating the
retrieval choice, rather than assuming that more context improves the graph.
\citep{v12_la_2402_15301}
Compare the assistant with ordinary search plus an economist and, where
its assumptions fit, a numerical discovery procedure. The inputs must
be matched. Assess false orientations, missed common causes and the
resulting effect or action, rather than relying solely on edge counts.

The first assistant should propose a diagram and competing explanations
for review, then call a named discovery or identification method under
explicit assumptions. Numerical discovery contributes its own evidence;
textual plausibility cannot turn an unresolved equivalence class into
a validated graph. The three-model pricing example is a useful adverse
case because one unjustified orientation changes the financial sign.

\section{A positive workflow result and its limits}
The retained ORCA study gives a more direct reason to test assistance in a
completed workflow. Twelve participants used a counterbalanced within-subjects
design; the baseline assistant already had tools, step gates and minimal
state. The paper's Figure 5 reports total task durations of 1,395 seconds
for the baseline and 1,107 seconds for ORCA, a reported reduction of about
21\%. Table 1 reports completion rates 0.75 and 0.83. This is positive
published evidence for a structured workflow on the study's relational,
generated causal tasks. It is not a measured benefit for this banking
proposal. \citep[pp.~3--5]{exec13_census_orca}

The interpretation changes when the outcome definitions and all attempted
analyses are retained. Completion means producing an ATE, regardless of
accuracy; discovery success requires the treatment and outcome nodes to be
present. The paper's confidence-interval metric is described as an estimated
ATE falling within a ground-truth interval, so its reported 0.083 and 0.50
must not be presented as conventional repeated-sample confidence coverage.
The full-data condition comparison for absolute ATE error has $p=0.321$;
after excluding configuration-error outliers, the reported OLS comparison
has $p=0.020$. Both belong in an assessment of completed work because
configuration errors are among the failures a service is supposed to avoid.
The abstract's claimed 42-percentage-point completion gain also differs
from the displayed 0.75-to-0.83 comparison; this synthesis uses the stated
table comparison rather than reconciling that discrepancy by invention.
\citep[pp.~1, 5, 17--18]{exec13_census_orca}

question clarification save full effort while preserving scientific quality.
It should retain all configuration failures and report separately the time
spent by the analyst, tool execution and correction. The external study
supports that experiment's plausibility. Its small participant sample,
specified tasks, outcome definitions and analysis exclusions prevent a
claim that the same benefit is established across bank studies.

\section{Identification, execution and reporting}
CLadder evaluates formal causal questions under constructed mechanisms;
its reported results concern historical models and that supplied task.
It does not measure elicitation of a new bank mechanism.
\citep{v12_la_2312_04350}
For identification, compare assistance with a defined formal procedure,
requiring the assistant to preserve both the answer and its conditions.
An appropriate refusal must explain the missing restriction, not simply
return an empty result. The benchmark literature and the retained
mechanism-clustering critiques give reasons to keep failed cases and
uncertainty denominators in the evaluation.

For execution, the existing local interface study shows equality for four
constructed requests, not model-driven analysis quality. A scripted
workflow is the credible baseline. Compare any assistant on request
construction, faithful tool use, errors detected and correction effort.
Do not give it credit for a calculation performed by the formal tool
while omitting the costs of choosing or correcting the request.

For reporting, a deterministic template is a strong comparator because
it can already state the estimand, assumptions, interval and scope.
The assistant's proposed value is explaining why the result changes a
decision or why it cannot yet support one. Check that explanation
against the actual result and the retained sources. A report that turns
a set crossing zero into a positive recommendation fails even if its
prose is persuasive. No local live-model evaluation establishes an
incremental benefit for this reporting task.

with evidence retrieval and explicit alternatives, evaluated against
the questionnaire. Identification and numerical results remain delegated
to defined procedures. Expansion to autonomous discovery, variable
construction or recommendations requires task-specific evidence. The
frontier census remains 82 inspected and 31 unread; this synthesis does
not claim those omissions have been resolved. A live comparison still
requires a fixed model version, held-out questions, matched information,
independent adjudication and a budget.

\chapter{The first investment and the evidence that would reverse it}
\label{rewrite:investment-decision}

The immediate proposal is a minimal comparative integration for a fixed
offer study, with explicit population weights, information dates and
a complete financial report. Reuse a transparent estimator and retain
a documented alternative. The seventeen-area comparison establishes
which further capabilities are plausible candidates and why they need
separate assumptions. It is not a reason to build all seventeen before
evaluating the first study.

\section{Compare equivalent completed studies}
There are four economically serious alternatives. Expert composition
uses existing methods and bespoke study documentation. Minimal integration
adds a reusable request and result description around selected methods.
A broad shared service adds more methods, languages, maintenance and
operating commitments. A commercial route can provide supported
procedures and existing institutional integration, but its relevant
entitlements, actual prices and matched capabilities are unknown here.
The detailed commercial discussions preserve documented features and
unknowns; an unobserved feature is not evidence that it is absent.

The proposed first comparison selects minimal integration against expert
composition. Its potential gains come from repeated target specification,
information-date checks, error detection and reporting. Fitting a regression
may occupy little of the total work. Any proposed saving must therefore
be measured over preparation, correction, interpretation and failed
attempts. Bespoke causal reasoning remains part of every alternative.

Let $N$ be annual studies genuinely eligible for this restricted route;
$h$ hours saved per completed study at equivalent quality; $w$ loaded
hourly cost; $D$ reduction in expected decision loss per study; $C$ annual
operating cost; and $K$ annualised development and adoption cost. Then
\[
 B=N(wh+D)-C-K.
\]
The conditional break-even study volume is $(C+K)/(wh+D)$ only when
$wh+D>0$. A negative denominator cannot be repaired by doing more studies.
The earlier illustrative investment account in Chapter~\ref{r3:investment}
retains its actual stipulated inputs and arithmetic, including the
26.74-study threshold. That threshold belongs to that account. It must
not be imported as an observed requirement for the newly selected scope.

The deposit example's \pounds3 population contribution concerns one
constructed customer action. It is not $D$, the improvement in decision
loss due to choosing one analytical workflow over another. Counting
that whole contribution as a software benefit would confuse policy value
with the incremental value of analysis. Similarly, correction hours
counted in $h$ must not be counted again in $D$. These distinctions
prevent an attractive worked example from becoming an invented ROI.

\section{A spending sequence with real alternatives}
The first expenditure buys a matched analyst comparison using the
constructed and public cases, with independently assessed scientific
quality and recorded full effort. It asks whether the small integration
changes decisions or reduces work enough to pay for its ongoing cost.
A bank-data pilot follows only if that evidence is favourable and the
bank supplies a defensible target, data access, assignment information
and a meaningful precision requirement. An operating trial then tests
the relevant interfaces and platform under its actual conditions.

Several observations would reverse or narrow the recommendation. Equal
quality and effort favour the established workflow. A commercial
entitlement supplying equivalent outputs at lower full cost favours
that route. Frequent lack of treatment support or reliable observation
truth favours better study design and data collection. A repeated
need for unsupported dependent inference limits the offer route rather
than justifying a broad claim. Evidence of consequential, reproducibly
avoided errors or lower full effort can justify extending the integration.

This is a conditional proposal with a selected next experiment. It
preserves the larger scientific and software programme without treating
its unfinished questions as already solved. The detailed comparisons
and operating evidence that follow allow a reader to inspect those
restrictions and alternatives before funding the next step.

A request to improve retention is not yet an intervention. An economist needs

baseline: if it obtains the same defensible question more cheaply, it should
be preferred. Assistance earns its cost when it discovers a material omission,
finds relevant evidence or reduces correction time.

\chapter{When repeated readings add information}
\label{gap29:measurement}

A bank may ask an assistant to recover financial distress from customer
notes before assessing the effect of a servicing action. Reading the same
notes several times is attractive because disagreement is easy to observe.
Agreement can be less informative: several readers may share the same
omission. The distinction affects whether text can help control confounding.
The literature on text-based causal adjustment identifies measurement error,
collider information and post-treatment content as separate problems.
\citep{exec13_census_text_review_arxiv}

\section{A common error creates a lower limit}
Consider a project model, not an empirical claim about any language model.
Let latent distress be $U$, the action index $A=U+\varepsilon_A$, and
the outcome $Y=\tau A+U+\varepsilon_Y$, with $\tau=-1/5$. The latent
variable and the two disturbances are independent, centred, unit-variance
Gaussians. Suppose reading $j$ produces $W_j=U+e_j$. The measurement errors
are independent of $U,\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_Y$, have variance $s$ and
equal pairwise correlation $\rho$. These premises make the calculation
transparent; actual extraction errors may violate all of them.

The averaged reading has error variance
\[
 s_m=\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=1}^m e_j\right)
     =s\left(\rho+\frac{1-\rho}{m}\right).
\]
The covariance of $(A,\overline W)$ is
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2&1\\1&1+s_m\end{smallmatrix}\right)$,
and its covariance with $Y$ is $(2\tau+1,\tau+1)'$. Solving these two
normal equations gives the coefficient on $A$ after adjustment:
\[

\chapter{The investment case and its alternatives}
\label{r3:investment}

A common causal product earns its cost by improving repeated scientific
work. The appropriate alternative is a capable quantitative team composing
the same open-source methods with ordinary engineering, documentation and
review. Such a team can produce good causal studies without a new platform.
The investment question is whether the shared representations and qualified
operations reduce the cost of equivalent work or enable additional valuable
decisions, after construction, support and adoption are included.

\section{Define equivalent output before pricing reuse}
\label{r3:equivalent-output}

An equivalent completed study has a reconstructed population and observation
clock, a clear intervention and financial outcome, a defensible identification
argument or useful nonidentification conclusion, appropriate inference,
reproducible artifacts and review. The comparison must include negative
results. An early finding that a requested target is unidentified can save
substantial work; forcing every study to return a numerical effect would
reward scientific error.

The proposed service would help analysts reconstruct what was known when
a decision was made, keep the population and outcome consistent, document
why an effect is identified, and carry uncertainty into the financial
comparison. It would reuse existing numerical methods where their
assumptions fit. Each business would still specify its products, costs and
constraints. A mortgage policy, an individual collections decision and a
macroeconomic shock need not share the same economic quantity of interest.

Comparator costs should include the same required outputs and review
quality. Reduced effort from omitting uncertainty or failing to investigate
weak support is not a saving. Conversely, building a generic model interface
for a one-off study can cost more than a small, clearly documented expert
analysis. The portfolio of genuinely repeated requests, not the total
number of database rows, determines the economic opportunity.

\section{An auditable cost model}
\label{r3:cost-model}

For alternative $j\in\{E,P\}$, expert composition or shared product,

$c_j$ marginal cost per equivalent completed study, and $n_t$ completed
studies in year $t$. With horizon $H$ and discount rate $r$,
\begin{equation}
 C_j=K_j+\sum_{t=1}^{H}\frac{F_j+c_jn_t}{(1+r)^t}.
 \label{r3:present-cost}
\end{equation}
The categories are disjoint: method maintenance and common infrastructure
belong in $F_j$, while study-specific preparation, fitting, review and
rework belong in $c_j$. Failed-study costs must be included in one
category; a completed-study denominator cannot make them disappear.

break-even logic:

or enterprise vendor quotations. Let

threshold, when $c_E>c_P$, is
\begin{equation}

\chapter{Servicing decisions change the next decision's information}
\label{rewrite:servicing}

A servicing policy chooses whether to contact a borrower at two dates. Let

state observed between contacts. For this constructed example, $Y$ is
gross contribution in pounds over the two-period horizon, excluding contact
cost. The policy comparison is sustained contact versus no contact, not
the regression coefficient of one contact conditional on every later event.

The exact law developed in Chapter~\ref{r3:longitudinal} is
\begin{align*}
 P(L_0=1)&=0.5,\\
 P(A_0=1\mid L_0)&=0.2+0.6L_0,\\
 P(L_1=1\mid L_0,A_0)&=0.1+0.5L_0+0.2A_0,\\
 P(A_1=1\mid H_1)&=0.15+0.5L_1+0.1A_0,\\

\end{align*}
Here $H_1=(L_0,A_0,L_1)$ is the history available for the second action.
Independent innovations implement these kernels. The actions have support
for every possible history, and the example has no hidden confounding.
Consequently, replacing both action kernels with a specified policy and
retaining the state-transition law identifies its mean. This is the

and its primary treatment. \citep[Chapter 21]{hernan2020}

\[

\]
The gross means are \pounds26.50 and \pounds35.50. At a stipulated

The reported exact enumeration independently averages the finite state law

does not repair the analysis: the historical second action depends on it.

ideas; their longitudinal scores, nuisance restrictions and remainders are
derived in Chapter~\ref{r3:longitudinal}, rather than assumed from their

uncertainty or an honest evaluation sample. An outcome law conditional on
a hidden state introduces another identification problem; a well-fitting

observable histories, retaining a direct g-computation and a weighting

\chapter{A learned graph can leave the pricing decision unresolved}
\label{rewrite:discovery}

Suppose $X$ measures a proposed rate change in percentage points, $M$ an
intermediate market quantity and $Y$ gross funding contribution in thousands
of pounds. The units and coefficients in this section are authored for the
example. Consider the centered Gaussian observational covariance
\[
 \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}
 1&0.6&0.48\\0.6&1.36&1.088\\0.48&1.088&1.8704
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
The law satisfies $X\perp Y\mid M$. A chain $X\to M\to Y$, a
fork $X\leftarrow M\to Y$, and a reverse chain $X\leftarrow M\leftarrow Y$
can all reproduce it using independent Gaussian errors.

For the first chain, take $M=0.6X+\varepsilon_M$ and
$Y=0.8M+\varepsilon_Y$, with variances $\Var(X)=1$,
$\Var(\varepsilon_M)=1$ and $\Var(\varepsilon_Y)=1$. The intervention
slope of $Y$ on $X$ is $0.6(0.8)=0.48$. For the fork, take

with residual variances $1-0.6^2/1.36$ and $1$. The resulting covariance

orientation that determines the action. A probability for each graph would
require additional justified modelling; equal probabilities are not supplied
by observational equivalence. Nor should the discrete set be called a
confidence interval. It represents identification ambiguity even if the
covariance is known exactly.

both the observed law and the retained models before mapping them to effects.
An edge bootstrap conditional on one chosen graph does not supply that
combined guarantee. The foundations and detailed temporal-discovery
comparisons retain the arguments for unresolved orientations, latent causes
and class-to-effect propagation.

that excludes two orientations, a valid instrument, or an intervention on
$X$. The cost of obtaining that information should be compared with the
consequence of a mistaken action. More precise estimation of this same
covariance cannot distinguish these three laws. The proposed service should
therefore preserve a class or explicit refusal and ask what would narrow it,
instead of completing arrows solely to make a diagram look decisive.

\chapter{Choosing the capabilities worth assembling}
\label{scisyn:software}

A bank does not buy an average treatment effect. It buys a better decision:
which customers to contact, which price to quote, which branches to reorganise,
or which experiment to fund. Software is useful when its answer bears on that
decision and its assumptions are credible in the setting. A method that answers
a narrower question accurately can be more valuable than an ambitious system
whose output is difficult to interpret.

proposal should assemble a small number of named statistical procedures around

FCI and different graph representations. An algorithmic orientation conflict

\citep{v12_sw_causallearn,exec13_pcalg_reuse_primary}

orientation would instead report an unidentified effect as identified. This is a rejection of an inference, not of a software

\section{Estimating benefits from actions and repeated policies}

\subsection{5. Average and heterogeneous effects}
EconML's residual-regression formulation illustrates why the final effect model
matters as much as the prediction methods used to remove confounding. In a
binary-treatment setting with sufficient observed adjustment information $S$,
write $e(S)=P(A=1\mid S)$ and $\tau(S)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid S]$. With exact nuisance
functions and a constant final coefficient, the population projection is
\[
 \theta_* = \frac{E[e(S)\{1-e(S)\}\tau(S)]}
                   {E[e(S)\{1-e(S)\}]}.
\]
The average benefit for the target population is instead $E[\tau(S)]$.
These coincide under a constant effect, but need not do so otherwise. This
derivation concerns a restricted specification, not every EconML estimator.
\citep{exec19_econml_source}

An explicit specification separates adjustment variables, effect modifiers
and population weights before an existing estimator is used.
R forest and targeted-estimation routes and Python DML routes should be compared
on the same population and intervention, not on their default output names.
The inspected grf source gives a concrete R/native reference, while commercial
Stata CATE procedures provide an additional documented comparator.
\citep{exec13_grf_rpath,exec13_ch_stata}
The proposed service's contribution is to make these choices visible and
repeatable. It has not demonstrated predictive or causal superiority over the
existing estimators. The generated study in Chapter~\ref{scisyn:evidence} examines
the decision consequence of an omitted effect modifier.

Eligibility rules, capacity limits and randomised offers can supply stronger
designs than adjustment alone. The inspected commercial IV manuals and
rdrobust sources provide useful estimation and diagnostic comparators.

requires an argument about the outcome, and a discontinuity requires a
credible comparison at the threshold. Bias correction for an RD estimate does
not establish a strong first stage for a fuzzy design.
\citep{exec13_ivrd_stata,exec13_ivrd_sas,exec13_ivrd_rdrobust}

Integrate the design-specific procedure already used by the research team
before commissioning a general replacement. Match the threshold, bandwidth,
polynomial, kernel, treatment definition and uncertainty calculation in any
cross-language comparison. Preserve weak or uninformative conclusions. Reject
automatic conversion of an instrument coefficient into a portfolio-wide
effect without an argument connecting the relevant population. The first
investment is usually a better account of eligibility and assignment, not a
second two-stage least-squares solver.

\subsection{7. Longitudinal actions, survival and competing events}
A collections policy changes future customer condition and future treatment.
Adjustment for a condition caused by an earlier action can therefore change
the estimand. The retained R gfoRmula and Python pygformula implementations
provide inspectable simulation and resampling paths for specified longitudinal
interventions. Their histories, event ordering and competing-event options
must be compared explicitly. They are not equivalent to fitting a hazard
regression with a time-varying covariate.
\citep{exec20_gformula_reuse,exec24_longpy_pygformula_source,exec14_survival_sas,
exec14_survival_stata_competing}

or death prevents the outcome being observed or is itself part of the outcome.

question from one that leaves it possible. Java and C++ survival components
can be useful computational ingredients, but the proposal does not infer a
complete sequential causal method from a survival routine. The unresolved
comparison is whether the entire policy, observation and uncertainty calculation
survives the chosen route, not whether it returns a plausible curve.

\subsection{8. Learning and evaluating a policy}
A policy assigns an action using information available at the decision date.

outcomes rewards chance as well as merit. The inspected R policytree source
optimises supplied action scores; the sources for dynamic-regime packages
address different histories and decision sequences. A commercial offline

interpretation.
\citep{exec24_policiesr_policytree,exec24_policiesr_dtrreg,
exec24_policiesr_polle,exec16_cp_bayesfusion,exec13_ch_stata}

\section{Changes across branches, markets and connected customers}

\subsection{9. Panel effects and staggered adoption}
The R did source distinguishes cohort, calendar, relative-time and treated-cell
aggregation. The inherited exact example has cohort shares $3/4$ and $1/4$;
the early cohort's effects are 2 and 4, and the late cohort's observed effect
is 10. The resulting aggregates are 4, $19/4$, 4 and $15/4$ for treated-cell,
group, dynamic and calendar targets respectively. None is an arithmetic error.
Their populations and time weights differ.
\citep{exec24_panelr_did}

Prefer a named group-time target and an explicit aggregation agreed with the
business owner. Compare R implementations with the inspected Python and
commercial panel routes only after matching the control population, treatment
timing, anticipatory period and uncertainty calculation. General fixed-effects
regression is an important comparator, not an automatic substitute for the
intended staggered-adoption target.

units to represent an otherwise unobserved trajectory under restrictions on
the outcome process and pre-intervention fit. Those restrictions need a
banking interpretation, including whether the proposed intervention affects
the donors.

vendor authorship or support for the extension. The R CausalImpact path is a

projections address different questions. The inspected Stata and EViews sources
provide concrete commercial comparators; they do not establish that a branch

\citep{exec19_dynamic_stata_ab,exec19_dynamic_stata_system,

specific decision about the first prototype.

Contacting one member of a household can affect another; a branch campaign can
shift business across nearby branches. The inspected MossSpider and
inferference sources implement different network and grouped-allocation
constructions. Their eligible populations, exposure definitions and uncertainty
calculations cannot be harmonised by renaming columns.
\citep{exec24_interference_mossspider,exec24_interference_inferference}

payment plan. The total effect of the policy and the effect of intervening on

distinguishes model and inference routes.
\citep{exec24_mediation_original,exec24_mediation_sources}

analysis presented beside the estimate. Retain controlled and natural effects
as different interventions. A commercial mediation command is a useful
comparator only after the treatment, mediator, population and scale are aligned.
\citep{exec13_ci_stata_mediate,exec20_med_stata_multiple}

bank funds. If the same action is preferred across the credible sensitivity

Successful results from one branch need not transfer to another. Causal

The retained transportability argument and commercial imputation manuals
support this distinction.
\citep{pearltransport2014,exec21_transport_stata_mi,
exec21_transport_sas_mi_intro,exec21_transport_sas_mianalyze_intro}

Integrate imputation and target-population weighting as explicit, separately
justified operations. Report which outcome and assignment information is
missing and why it is believed recoverable. An imputed column does not recover
an unrecorded treatment policy or the potential outcome of a systematically
excluded population. Preserve adverse sensitivity results. Commercial systems
already provide substantial missing-data facilities; the proposed service's
candidate advantage is a clearer causal interpretation and repeatable
comparison, which still needs evaluation. No new universal solution to
unmeasured selection is claimed.

\section{Computation and the observations on which inference rests}

\subsection{15. Bayesian and hidden-state models}
Posterior computation is valuable when an economic model distinguishes hidden
credit condition from noisy observations. It quantifies uncertainty conditional
on the model and prior. It does not establish the restrictions that give a
policy intervention its meaning. The inspected Bayesian and factor-inference
sources therefore belong in a different category from observational graph
identification.
\citep{exec23_pymc_sources,exec25_bsw_stan,exec24_libdai_source,
exec22_state_stata_bayesmh,exec22_state_stata_sspace_post}

Reuse a mature inference engine for a model that can be explained economically.
Keep prior sensitivity, convergence diagnostics, observation timing and
structural uncertainty visible. A posterior with narrow intervals can remain
conditional on restrictions the bank cannot verify. Prefer established R,
Python or C++ computation over a new sampler unless the model demands an
unavailable operation. Commercial graphical engines remain conditional
comparators, with numerical inference and causal identification assessed
separately.

\subsection{16. Identity, ownership and information dates}
Before a policy effect is estimated, records must represent the intended
customer, institution and decision date. The retained DuckDB, Feast and Polars
sources provide useful tools for queries, historical features and joins.
Their technical functionality cannot establish that a record was available
to a decision-maker merely because its economic event date is earlier.
\citep{exec19_duckdb_source,exec19_feast_source,exec23_polars_sources}

Adopt data-processing components, while retaining event time, publication time
and the time a corrected value became available. Validate ownership changes and
identity links against the particular target. A rare incorrect link can have
a large monetary consequence if it involves a large exposure. The existing
public-data survey makes UCI Bank Marketing useful for a timing example:
call duration is unavailable when deciding whether to place the call. It does
not establish an effect of calling from a representative untreated group.
\citep{pd15_uci_bank}
Reject retrospective access to later information in a purported historical
decision. The unresolved requirement is credible observation history, not a
missing SQL function.

\subsection{17. Numerical computation and a reproducible study}
Java regression libraries, C++ numerical kernels and other-language panel
packages can reduce development effort. Their statistical surroundings matter.
The inspected C++ panel sources sit inside procedures that select samples,
define effects and scale uncertainty; a coefficient solver alone does not
preserve those steps. A Julia suite and its individual components likewise
must not be counted as independent corroborating implementations.
\citep{exec25_paneljava_commons,exec25_panelcxx_fixest,
exec25_panelcxx_xhdfe,exec25_panelother_julia}

Adopt general numerical components where they answer a defined computational
need. Integrate complete statistical procedures when their sample and inference
rules are material. Port only after a measured constraint makes the expected
benefit exceed development, comparison and maintenance costs. A study run
through a library, a command line or an assistant should preserve the same
question and result. Agent frameworks and vendor service clients may help
conduct the work, but a completed call is not evidence that a causal
interpretation is justified.
\citep{exec24_framework_contracts,exec23_workflow_sasctl}

\section{What the commercial comparison changes}
Commercial statistical packages are credible alternatives, not an empty space
waiting for the proposed service. The inspected Stata procedures cover distinct
treatment, panel, survival and structural questions; the SAS sources distinguish
statistical procedures from service access. The bank may already possess
trained staff and relevant entitlements. A proposal that ignores those assets
overstates the saving from a new platform.
\citep{exec13_ci_stata_causal_intro,exec18_gp_stata_xthdid,
exec14_survival_stata,exec13_ivrd_sas,exec23_workflow_sasctl}

Compare three feasible alternatives: improve existing analytical practice;
connect a small set of existing procedures; or build a broader common service.
For each study, distinguish a vendor-authored procedure, a community extension
inside a commercial host, an open client to a licensed server, and a general
numerical component. They have different support and cost implications. The
comparison has not established exact current prices, complete entitlements,
performance at the bank's scale or the absence of equivalent features in all
competitors. Those are unresolved commercial questions, not findings of
technical superiority.

The proposed investment is therefore conditional. Its candidate contribution
is a disciplined connection between the business question, assumptions,
software choices and financial interpretation. Fund a narrow comparison that
can show whether that connection prevents material errors or saves analyst
time. If the existing estate achieves the same result more cheaply, retain it.
If differences in estimands, graph interpretation or information dates repeatedly
change decisions, a shared service becomes more persuasive.

\section{What remains to be learned}
The seventeen areas now lead to explicit provisional choices, but this synthesis
does not complete the underlying census. There is no claim that every
language--area pair has been exhaustively searched or that every candidate has
been executed. Complete dated source and capability comparisons where a missing
candidate could change the preferred route. Compare actual implementations on
matched questions before claiming numerical agreement. Obtain edition,
entitlement and price information before a purchase recommendation. Investigate
transitive numerical details only where they could change the inference or
the selected integration.

Some limits require new information rather than more programming: unidentified
effects under unrestricted confounding, absent support for a proposed action,
unknown assignment histories and uncertain transfer to a new population. State
the restrictions or data that would narrow each limit. These findings can
support a useful proposal even when they do not support a universal product.

\section{Changes across branches, markets and connected customers}

\subsection{9. Panel effects and staggered adoption}
The R did source distinguishes cohort, calendar, relative-time and treated-cell
aggregation. The inherited exact example has cohort shares $3/4$ and $1/4$;
the early cohort's effects are 2 and 4, and the late cohort's observed effect
is 10. The resulting aggregates are 4, $19/4$, 4 and $15/4$ for treated-cell,
group, dynamic and calendar targets respectively. None is an arithmetic error.
Their populations and time weights differ.
\citep{exec24_panelr_did}

Prefer a named group-time target and an explicit aggregation agreed with the
business owner. Compare R implementations with the inspected Python and
commercial panel routes only after matching the control population, treatment
timing, anticipatory period and uncertainty calculation. General fixed-effects
regression is an important comparator, not an automatic substitute for the
intended staggered-adoption target.
\citep{exec20_fixest_source,exec24_panelpy_differences,exec18_gp_stata_xthdid}

unchanged label. Reusing an R or Python procedure through another language is
initially preferable to reproducing its entire aggregation and inference
logic around a generic regression solver.

\subsection{10. Synthetic controls and comparative time series}
For a small number of treated regions, donor suitability can matter more than
the choice of optimiser. The synthetic-control construction uses untreated
units to represent an otherwise unobserved trajectory under restrictions on
the outcome process and pre-intervention fit. Those restrictions need a
banking interpretation, including whether the proposed intervention affects
the donors.
\citep{abadie2010}

Document donor eligibility, outcome units, pre-period choice and the protocol

software hosted by a commercial product; licensing the host does not establish
vendor authorship or support for the extension. The R CausalImpact path is a
different model-based construction, with its own assumptions about controls
and stability.
\citep{exec19_synth_stata_source,exec13_ci_r,exec13_ci_semantics}

there is evidence of a material deployment advantage. The proposal should
compare sensitivity to donor and model choices before promising robust regional
savings.

shocks. Dynamic-panel instruments, structural VAR restrictions and local
projections address different questions. The inspected Stata and EViews sources
provide concrete commercial comparators; they do not establish that a branch
rate-setting policy is exogenous.
\citep{exec19_dynamic_stata_ab,exec19_dynamic_stata_system,
exec19_dynamic_stata_lp,exec19_dynamic_eviews_panel}

Integrate a model only with its instrument restrictions, horizon and sampling
unit. A large number of customer rows does not create a large number of
independent policy dates. Preserve the effective calendar and ask whether
uncertainty is driven by branches, common dates or both. Forecasting can be
valuable in its own right, but a forecast response to an input change does not
by itself justify changing a pricing rule. A new native implementation should
be considered only after the instrument and dependence comparison changes a
specific decision about the first prototype.

Contacting one member of a household can affect another; a branch campaign can
shift business across nearby branches. The inspected MossSpider and
inferference sources implement different network and grouped-allocation
constructions. Their eligible populations, exposure definitions and uncertainty
calculations cannot be harmonised by renaming columns.
\citep{exec24_interference_mossspider,exec24_interference_inferference}

For an initial study, choose one economic exposure and one defensible assignment
mechanism. Preserve the population of outcomes separately from the population
of possible recipients. Integrate the matching statistical method and retain
a no-spillover analysis as a deliberately restrictive comparator. Generic Java
or C++ network libraries can represent relationships or simulate a supplied
process; that is not evidence that they identify an effect in the observed
bank network. Reject the claim that connectivity alone resolves interference.

the economically relevant links, not a faster graph traversal.

A policy may improve repayment through contact, understanding and a revised
payment plan. The total effect of the policy and the effect of intervening on
one of those mechanisms are different quantities. The retained R mediation
paper explicitly distinguishes the additional assumptions needed for causal
mediation; randomising treatment alone does not settle them. The source also
distinguishes model and inference routes.
\citep{exec24_mediation_original,exec24_mediation_sources}

analysis presented beside the estimate. Retain controlled and natural effects
as different interventions. A commercial mediation command is a useful
comparator only after the treatment, mediator, population and scale are aligned.
\citep{exec13_ci_stata_mediate,exec20_med_stata_multiple}

For the investment decision, ask whether the mechanism would change what the
bank funds. If the same action is preferred across the credible sensitivity
range, a more elaborate decomposition may have little immediate value.

Successful results from one branch need not transfer to another. Causal
transport requires assumptions linking the source and target populations;
filling missing values within the source population is a separate task.
The retained transportability argument and commercial imputation manuals
support this distinction.
\citep{pearltransport2014,exec21_transport_stata_mi,
exec21_transport_sas_mi_intro,exec21_transport_sas_mianalyze_intro}

justified operations. Report which outcome and assignment information is
missing and why it is believed recoverable. An imputed column does not recover
an unrecorded treatment policy or the potential outcome of a systematically
excluded population. Preserve adverse sensitivity results. Commercial systems
already provide substantial missing-data facilities; the proposed service's
candidate advantage is a clearer causal interpretation and repeatable
comparison, which still needs evaluation. No new universal solution to
unmeasured selection is claimed.

\subsection{15. Bayesian and hidden-state models}
Posterior computation is valuable when an economic model distinguishes hidden
credit condition from noisy observations. It quantifies uncertainty conditional
on the model and prior. It does not establish the restrictions that give a
policy intervention its meaning. The inspected Bayesian and factor-inference
sources therefore belong in a different category from observational graph

not establish an effect of calling from a representative untreated group.

define effects and scale uncertainty; a coefficient solver alone does not
preserve those steps. A Julia suite and its individual components likewise

\citep{exec25_paneljava_commons,exec25_panelcxx_fixest,
exec25_panelcxx_xhdfe,exec25_panelother_julia}

question and result. Agent frameworks and vendor service clients may help

interpretation is justified.

\section{What the commercial comparison changes}

treatment, panel, survival and structural questions; the SAS sources distinguish
statistical procedures from service access. The bank may already possess

does not complete the underlying census. There is no claim that every
language--area pair has been exhaustively searched or that every candidate has

\chapter{Choosing the capabilities worth assembling}
\label{scisyn:software}

A bank does not buy an average treatment effect. It buys a better decision:
which customers to contact, which price to quote, which branches to reorganise,
or which experiment to fund. Software is useful when its answer bears on that
decision and its assumptions are credible in the setting. A method that answers
a narrower question accurately can be more valuable than an ambitious system
whose output is difficult to interpret.

The detailed comparisons in this monograph support selective reuse. The first
proposal should assemble a small number of named statistical procedures around
a common description of the decision. It should retain a second implementation
where disagreement could expose a consequential mistake. It should not promise
to reproduce every package in one language. The development expense of such a
rewrite is certain; the benefit remains to be demonstrated.

The comparison below draws on the retained technical sources and their dated
versions. It is a synthesis of those inspections, not a new census of current
releases. Research coverage ends on 7 October 2026; acquisition after that date
does not establish historical availability of a mutable manual. A documented
procedure, an executed example and a proposed integration are different kinds
of evidence. Commercial tools are compared by their documented procedures;
unobserved functions remain unknown rather than being treated as absent.

\section{Discovering relationships and identifying effects}

\subsection{1. Discovery from independent observations}
For a cross-sectional customer study, the first choice is the set of assumptions
under which conditional independence or a score can reveal useful structure.
The inspected R pcalg, Python causal-learn and Java Tetrad implementations provide
concrete comparison routes for PC. They expose choices about independence tests,
search and orientation. Using the same algorithm name does not align those
choices. A graph with unresolved directions is a legitimate result, not an
unfinished diagram to be completed by managerial intuition.
\citep{exec13_pcalg_reuse_primary,v12_sw_causallearn,exec13_java_tetrad}

A restricted PC comparison needs one primary implementation and another
whose choices can be inspected independently. The independence test, sampling
unit, significance level and treatment of orientation conflicts determine
whether their outputs can be compared.
Porting the search into a new language is not justified by the proposal's
present evidence. Score-based, functional and continuous-optimisation methods
belong beside PC as different modelling choices, rather than votes for a
majority graph. In particular, agreement among bridges to the same underlying
engine is not independent corroboration. The software recommendation changes
if the bank needs a mixed-data model, hidden common causes or repeated records:
those needs require a separate statistical comparison before an interface is
chosen.

\subsection{2. Hidden common causes, selection and equivalent graphs}
An apparent connection between contact and repayment may arise because staff
recognise distress that the database does not record. Under such circumstances
an analysis assuming no hidden common causes can be precise about the wrong
model. The inspected discovery sources distinguish procedures such as PC and
FCI and different graph representations. An algorithmic orientation conflict
must not be reinterpreted as an established hidden common cause merely because
the display uses a similar pair of arrowheads.
\citep{v12_sw_causallearn,exec13_pcalg_reuse_primary}

The partially directed or ancestral graph determines a range of intervention
conclusions under its stated assumptions. A latent-variable route also needs
an explicit interpretation of its endpoints. Selecting one convenient
orientation would instead report an unidentified effect as identified. This is a rejection of an inference, not of a software
family. Where observationally equivalent models imply different lending
decisions, additional timing knowledge or experimental information is the
valuable purchase. Another graph visualiser cannot supply that information.

\subsection{3. Time, interventions and changing regimes}
Repeated customer observations contain both persistence and common shocks.
The retained Tigramite sources distinguish discovery methods, tests, lag
conventions, graph classes and effect calculations conditional on a supplied
graph. Their observation and masking rules matter when a calendar period is
missing. A row after a missing month is not necessarily the next economic
period. Commercial dynamic-network and structural time-series routes are
useful alternatives, but a supplied temporal model and a discovered model
answer different questions.
\citep{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec13_ct_genie_dbn,exec13_ct_stata_svar}

Temporal integration therefore depends on the original calendar, observation
availability and the allowed intervention. Evidence from multiple regimes
has a different interpretation from an assumption that one stationary regime
describes all years. A rate change during a funding crisis need not have the response seen
in ordinary months. A lagged prediction improvement alone does not identify a general temporal
effect. The first comparison should assess whether plausible
lag and regime choices change the decision, with graph ambiguity carried into
the effect calculation.

\subsection{4. Adjustment, identification and counterfactual questions}
The bank must distinguish identification of an intervention distribution from
evaluation of a structural model that somebody has supplied. Ananke's inspected
identification and model-oracle interfaces make this distinction concrete.
aGrUM and pyAgrum likewise combine graphical, symbolic and numerical facilities
whose individual meanings must be preserved. A symbolic expression may still
require conditional distributions unsupported by the observed population.
\citep{exec24_ananke_source,exec19_cxx_identification_source,exec24_agrum_source}

Symbolic identification determines what can be learned before an estimator
is selected. Model-based counterfactual simulation answers a separate question
conditional on the supplied structure. A simulation from that structure
therefore cannot establish identification from observational records.
An R, Python or C++ route is acceptable only if it preserves the query,
conditioning set, hidden-variable assumptions and support requirements. The
unresolved commercial comparison concerns exact query semantics and supported
model classes; a capability label such as causal analysis is insufficient.

\section{Estimating benefits from actions and repeated policies}

\subsection{5. Average and heterogeneous effects}
EconML's residual-regression formulation illustrates why the final effect model
matters as much as the prediction methods used to remove confounding. In a
binary-treatment setting with sufficient observed adjustment information $S$,
write $e(S)=P(A=1\mid S)$ and $\tau(S)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid S]$. With exact nuisance
functions and a constant final coefficient, the population projection is
\[
 \theta_* = \frac{E[e(S)\{1-e(S)\}\tau(S)]}
                   {E[e(S)\{1-e(S)\}]}.
\]
The average benefit for the target population is instead $E[\tau(S)]$.
These coincide under a constant effect, but need not do so otherwise. This
derivation concerns a restricted specification, not every EconML estimator.
\citep{exec19_econml_source}

An explicit specification separates adjustment variables, effect modifiers
and population weights before an existing estimator is used.
R forest and targeted-estimation routes and Python DML routes should be compared
on the same population and intervention, not on their default output names.
The inspected grf source gives a concrete R/native reference, while commercial
Stata CATE procedures provide an additional documented comparator.
\citep{exec13_grf_rpath,exec13_ch_stata}
The proposed service's contribution is to make these choices visible and
repeatable. It has not demonstrated predictive or causal superiority over the
existing estimators. The generated study in Chapter~\ref{scisyn:evidence} examines
the decision consequence of an omitted effect modifier.

\subsection{6. Experiments, instruments and discontinuities}
Eligibility rules, capacity limits and randomised offers can supply stronger
designs than adjustment alone. The inspected commercial IV manuals and
rdrobust sources provide useful estimation and diagnostic comparators.
Their identifying premises remain substantive: a valid excluded instrument
requires an argument about the outcome, and a discontinuity requires a
credible comparison at the threshold. Bias correction for an RD estimate does
not establish a strong first stage for a fuzzy design.
\citep{exec13_ivrd_stata,exec13_ivrd_sas,exec13_ivrd_rdrobust}

An existing design-specific procedure gives the research team an informative
baseline. A cross-language comparison is interpretable only with the same
threshold, bandwidth, polynomial, kernel, treatment definition and uncertainty
calculation. A weak or uninformative result may be correct. Converting an
instrument coefficient into a portfolio-wide effect instead requires an
additional argument connecting the relevant population. The first
investment is usually a better account of eligibility and assignment, not a
second two-stage least-squares solver.

\subsection{7. Longitudinal actions, survival and competing events}
A collections policy changes future customer condition and future treatment.
Adjustment for a condition caused by an earlier action can therefore change
the estimand. The retained R gfoRmula and Python pygformula implementations
provide inspectable simulation and resampling paths for specified longitudinal
interventions. Their histories, event ordering and competing-event options
must be compared explicitly. They are not equivalent to fitting a hazard
regression with a time-varying covariate.
\citep{exec20_gformula_reuse,exec24_longpy_pygformula_source,exec14_survival_sas,
exec14_survival_stata_competing}

A complete longitudinal procedure follows whole customer histories. Its
meaning depends on whether default, repayment, account closure or death
prevents observation or constitutes part of the outcome itself.
An intervention that eliminates a competing event is a different business
question from one that leaves it possible. Java and C++ survival components
can be useful computational ingredients, but the proposal does not infer a
